tasks.instruction: Return the index of the first of the four bins whose stock is at least the threshold, scanning all four bins, or 4 when no bin qualifies.
tasks.note: Start caps the scan at three steps, so an all-short array returns 3; a count of 5 overshoots to 5.

tasks.instruction: The burn amount and the fuel reserve are passed to the burn loop in the wrong order; pass them so each burn uses the burn amount and stops before fuel would drop below the reserve.
tasks.note: Parameters are fuel, burn, reserve. Burns = min(10, floor((fuel-reserve)/burn)). Wrong edit fixes the order but caps the loop at 5.

tasks.instruction: Return the length of the opening run of samples that are on the same side of 50 as the first sample (above 50 counts as on); the run can be at most all six samples.
tasks.note: The scan starts at index 1, so only 5 steps fit; with 6 the index wraps to 0 and a uniform array gives 7. Compares two bools with eq.

tasks.instruction: Return how many of the four monthly bills can be paid in order before the running total would exceed the budget; all four months must be considered.
tasks.note: Two fixes: loop count 4 and returning the month field (0) instead of the total paid (1).

tasks.instruction: The number of jumps must be capped by the third parameter instead of always allowing up to eight jumps.
tasks.note: Parameters: start square, board end, jump cap. Each jump goes to 2s+1 while the square is before the end.

tasks.instruction: The search for a free slot (a zero bit in the busy mask) must begin at the slot given by the second parameter, not at slot 0.
tasks.note: At most 8 slots are checked; when all are busy the result is start + 8.

tasks.instruction: Count halvings only while the amplitude is strictly above the threshold, so counting stops as soon as it is at or below the threshold; the helpers stay unchanged.
tasks.note: The predicate is ge; amp > thr is amp >= thr+1, so the fix passes threshold+1 to the loop. Thresholds near 2^32-1 are not tested.

tasks.instruction: Return the index of the last of the four slots that holds the key, searching from the end, or 4294967295 when the key is absent.
tasks.note: Start begins at index 4, which wraps to slot 0 on the first check. Compares a bool with false via eq.

tasks.instruction: Vowels are numbered from 1, so 1 must give the byte of 'a', 5 the byte of 'u', and numbers keep cycling through the five vowels.
tasks.note: 0 - 1 wraps to 4294967295, which is 0 mod 5, so 0 gives 'a'.

tasks.instruction: Day numbers now start with Sunday as 0 (Monday 1, ..., Saturday 6, then repeating); return the capital initial of that day.
tasks.note: Index wraps mod 7. Shifting by one with the old text is the wrong direction (needs +6).

tasks.instruction: Add all four bytes of the tag to the seed (not just the first three), then keep only the low 8 bits of the result.
tasks.note: RCPT = 82,67,80,84; sum 313 (first three 229). Result (seed+313) & 255.

tasks.instruction: Make the comparison case-insensitive: a lowercase letter byte must also match the capital letter stored at that position of the banner.
tasks.note: Clearing bit 5 (and 223) maps lowercase to uppercase and leaves uppercase alone; subtracting 32 breaks uppercase input.

tasks.instruction: Count how often the byte occurs only in the last four letters of the word, instead of in the whole word.
tasks.note: TICKETS = 84,73,67,75,69,84,83; last four are K,E,T,S (offset 3, count 4). Offset 4 wraps to the first T.

tasks.instruction: Pick the glyph by whole quarters of the percentage (0-24 first glyph, 25-49 second, 50-74 third, 75-99 fourth, 100 the last); currently 100 wraps back to the first glyph.
The input reading is in tenths; write it converted to whole units, rounding down.
tasks.note: Only one word is read.

tasks.instruction: Read two words and write them in the opposite order: the second word first, then the first word.
tasks.note: Missing input reads as 0.

tasks.instruction: Read the next three input words (not two) and write their sum.
tasks.note: Sum wraps mod 2^32. Wrong edit reads the third word but adds the second twice.

tasks.instruction: The posted array must also hold the total of the two scores as a third element, after the two scores.
tasks.note: puts writes the length first. Writing the total separately gives length 2.

tasks.instruction: The status tag must be written before the code, not after it; both must still be written.
tasks.note: The helper puts the text OK = [79,75] with its length 2.

tasks.instruction: Read a second word as well and emit the first word times the factor, plus the second word.
tasks.note: Token passes through the earlier helper emit. Wrong edit multiplies the sum.

tasks.instruction: Read two words and write the larger of the two.
tasks.note: Start writes the smaller word.

tasks.instruction: Log the two readings newest first: the second word read, then the first.
tasks.note: Token goes through the earlier helper log_pair, which puts the array (length 2 first).

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that computes the late fee from the days late (5 plus 2 per day when at least one day late, otherwise 0), and make the total use it instead of the flat 5.
tasks.note: New helper written before total_due. Wrong helper charges a fee on day 0.

tasks.instruction: Replace the plain average with a weighted one where the middle sample counts twice, (first + 2*middle + last) / 4 rounded down, computed in a new helper that smooth calls.
tasks.note: Wrong edit passes the samples to the helper in the wrong order, doubling the last sample.

tasks.instruction: Hours above 40 are paid at double rate; add a helper that returns the hours above 40 (0 when 40 or fewer) and use it in the pay calculation.
tasks.note: Pay = hours*rate + overtime*rate. Without the guard the helper wraps below 40 hours.

tasks.instruction: Compare the minimum against available stock, which is stock minus reserved (0 when more is reserved than in stock), computed by a new helper; ordering stays off while paused.
tasks.note: Parameters: stock, reserved, minimum, paused. Compares a bool to false with eq.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that says whether the hour is in the maintenance window (hours 2 and 3 inclusive), and report a fault only when the two sensors disagree outside that window.
tasks.note: Compares bools with ne and eq. Wrong helper excludes hour 3.

tasks.instruction: Round the total (unit cents times quantity) up to the next multiple of 5 cents, using a new helper that does the rounding; exact multiples stay unchanged.
tasks.note: Adding 5 instead of 4 bumps exact multiples up by 5.
